children.text: A lagoon hidden on Bucas Grande Island, southwest of Siargao: once you pass a cave entrance that can be entered only when the tide is out, a lake ringed by limestone peaks opens up. With a stingless jellyfish lake, caves that glow blue and cliff jumps, it is a popular adventure day trip from Siargao.

Sohoton Cove is a cluster of limestone islets off the southwest of Bucas Grande Island, which belongs to the municipality of Socorro in Surigao del Norte. Bucas Grande covers about 128 km² and lies across Dapa Channel, southwest of Siargao, and Socorro is an island municipality whose territory is contiguous with it (14 barangays, about 28,000 people in 2024). "Sohoton" is said to mean
narrow opening
in Visayan, a name that came from the narrow waterways between the small islands. It only sounds like
Sohoton Natural Bridge National Park
on Samar, which is a different place.

The key to this place is its entrance. The only way into the lagoon is a low cave passage beneath a cliff; small boats can pass only when the water is low, and when the tide comes in the entrance is submerged. Beyond it lies a quiet turquoise lake ringed by seven jungle-covered limestone peaks. In and around the lagoon are Hagukan Cave, which you swim into only at low tide, Magkukuob Cave, where you jump out through an opening at the top of a cliff, Crystal Cave, which you walk into, Tojoman Lagoon, home to stingless spotted jellyfish, and the deep blue Tiktikan Lagoon.

The area is said to fall within the Siargao Island Protected Landscape and Seascape (SIPLAS), and on-site registration and a guide are mandatory. Nepenthes merrilliana pitcher plants grow in the limestone forest, and tarsiers and hornbills are said to live there, though visitors rarely see them. Visitors to Socorro grew from about 4,000 in 2010 to more than 50,000 in 2017, then fell with the pandemic and Typhoon Odette in 2021, and in October 2023 dropped to about 1,000 after reports about a local group. As of 2026, tours from Siargao are on sale as normal.
Most people visit on a day tour by boat from General Luna. The round-trip boat ride alone takes around
3–5 hours

and can be bumpy, but in one day you can take in the caves, the lagoon, the jellyfish lake and the cliff jumps. It suits travelers who can swim and enjoy getting wet; if you are uneasy in tight, enclosed spaces or at heights, skip the riskier parts and enjoy the scenery from the boat, which is still well worth the trip.

blocks.title: The low-tide cave entrance and the lagoon of seven peaks

children.text: After registering at the Sohoton tourist center on the Socorro side, you pass through the low cave entrance in a small boat steered by your guide. Inside, seven limestone peaks ring the lake. One of them is said to be called the Cathedral because a sound like a bell was once heard there.

blocks.title: Hagukan Cave — the cave where the water glows blue

children.text: You can enter only when the water is low; at high tide the entrance is submerged. Swim through a small gap and you reach a deep pool beneath a domed ceiling with stalactites, and when you splash, the water is said to glow blue. It also goes by the nickname "Snoring Cave," because the waves are said to make a snoring-like sound as they flow in and out.

blocks.title: Magkukuob Cave — climb up from inside and jump from the cliff

children.text: Swim in through a small entrance, wade through waist-deep water and climb the rocks, and you reach an exit at the top of a cliff. Jumping from this exit into the lagoon, a drop of about
5 m
, is the finale of the course. It is very dark even with a flashlight, so if you are not confident, it is fine just to watch from the entrance.
A small boat from the registration area takes about
5–10 minutes
to reach a lake where spotted jellyfish (Mastigias papua), brown with white spots, drift. They do not sting, but you must not touch them or lift them out of the water. Numbers peak in
March–June
and are low in other months.

These are limestone caves you walk into with a guide, with bats, swiftlet nests and icicle-shaped stalactites. Deeper inside, a narrow tube-like passage runs for hundreds of meters, so it is not for anyone with claustrophobia. Bolitas Cave has to be crawled through, and entry and guide fees are about
Walk about
5 minutes

over the hill behind Club Tara and Sohoton Gamay Resort and you reach a deep blue lake. Surrounded by jungle and cliffs, it is quiet, and you can rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards. It is regarded as the most peaceful stop of the day.
Sohoton Gamay Resort and Club Tara have diving boards about
5 m
high, and at the rock of Hagukan Cave you can jump from a similar height. Jump only where the guide has checked the water depth and the rocks, and if it is your first time, start from a lower spot.

blocks.title: The lagoon early in the morning and at sunset

children.text: Day-tour groups start to crowd the place from around 9 a.m. If you stay overnight on the Sohoton side, you can see the lagoon at its quietest before the groups arrive, and enjoy the sunset.

At the Sohoton tourist center, you move around inside the lagoon in a small pump boat run by a local guide, and to Tojoman Jellyfish Lagoon in a small paddle boat. The pump boat and guide inside the lagoon are quoted at about
per boat and the paddle boat to the jellyfish lake at about
per person; these are often included in the tour price, so check item by item when you book. Tiktikan Lagoon and Crystal Cave are reached on foot.
Because you have a long sea crossing by boat, the dry season,
March–October
, when the waves are calm, is the safer choice. Jellyfish are most numerous in
March–June
because they live only about 4 months (some sources say
February–June
, or as late as
September
), and as this is also the peak season, it gets crowded.
July–October
has occasional showers but is relatively quiet, with fewer jellyfish, so keep in mind that their numbers vary from year to year. Socorro's annual rainfall is about 1,988 mm.
From
November–February

, the northeast monsoon roughs up the strait, many tours are cancelled, and high water may keep you out of some caves. The most important factor is the tide. Hagukan Cave can be entered only when the water is low, and the lagoon entrance is also said to be submerged at high tide, so departure times are set by the tide table. children.text: Prices are rough estimates for
and may vary with local conditions.
Most travelers stay in General Luna on Siargao and come back the same day. General Luna has everything from hostels to boutique resorts, at about
per night. If you want to sleep near Sohoton, choose an island stay on the Socorro side such as Club Tara Resort (overwater bungalows), Hidden Island Resort or Sohoton Bay Resort. A night costs about
, and some cottages run by community groups are cheaper. Facilities are basic and rooms are few, so book ahead.
There are almost no restaurants in Sohoton, so first check whether the tour includes lunch. An island restaurant meal package costs about
and comes with grilled fish, squid, shrimp, rice and tropical fruit. At a pier restaurant you can eat for around
. There are no shops or ATMs in Sohoton, so bring snacks, water and cash from General Luna.
When you book, check item by item whether the tour price includes the combined fee, the boat inside the lagoon, the jellyfish lake paddle boat and lunch, and have cash ready for any extras.
An early start is best. There is a long queue at registration and each lake has a time limit (about 20 minutes), so leaving around 6 a.m. and avoiding the peak season (
March–June
) and weekends makes for a much more relaxed day.
The boat ride is long and can be rough, so if you get seasick, take motion-sickness medicine
30 minutes
before departure.
You will get wet at the caves and jump spots, so a waterproof bag, a waterproof phone case and water shoes are essential. It is dark inside the caves, so a headlamp is handy.
Do not touch the jellyfish or lift them out of the water, and either skip sunscreen or use only reef-safe products.
If you are not a confident swimmer, wear a life jacket and just watch Hagukan and Magkukuob caves from the entrance. Jump only where your guide has checked.
There is no shade on the boat, so bring a long-sleeved rash guard, a hat and sunglasses.

The cave entrance and the lagoon entrance are submerged when the tide comes in. You must leave the lagoon within the time your guide sets, and swimming toward the entrance on your own or going into the caves without a guide is extremely dangerous.
Dives and jumps at Hagukan and Magkukuob caves must be done only on the instructions of a local guide who knows the water depth and the rocks. The Magkukuob exit and jump spot is about
5 m
high.

Whether swimming in the jellyfish lake is allowed seems to vary with the season and the guide. Some visitors report being kept out of the water because of sunscreen pollution, while recent guidance allows only quiet swimming and bans jumping in and splashing. Jellyfish numbers differ every year, so you may not see any.
The lagoon and the jellyfish lake are protected areas. Collecting coral or jellyfish, dumping trash and touching are banned, and a guide is mandatory.

Fees, visitor limits and whether the lake is open depend on decisions by the Socorro local government, so check the latest notices. The Socorro tourism office is listed as open daily 8 a.m.–noon and 1–5 p.m.

When the northeast monsoon is blowing or a typhoon is forecast, tours may be cancelled, and you should refuse any pushy offer to sail anyway. A big storm such as Typhoon Odette (Rai) in 2021 damages coral and facilities.
Mobile signal is weak for long stretches, which makes emergency calls difficult. Leave your schedule and contact details with your tour operator and lodging.
There are reports of sharks being kept in an enclosure around Crystal Cave, so avoid any experience that raises animal-welfare concerns.
